title: All Subsets
statement:
Produce every subset of a collection of distinct integers.

Contract
- `values` holds distinct integers (possibly negative) and may be empty.
- Return every subset exactly once, including the empty subset and the full set. A collection of k values has 2^k subsets.
- The order of the subsets and the order of the numbers inside a subset do not matter.
- Each returned subset must be its own list, and `values` must not be changed.

Examples
- `subsets(new int[]{1, 2, 3})` returns `[[], [1], [2], [3], [1, 2], [1, 3], [2, 3], [1, 2, 3]]` in any order.
- `subsets(new int[]{})` returns `[[]]`.
- `subsets(new int[]{5, -1})` returns `[[], [5], [-1], [5, -1]]` in any order.
hints: Every value is either in a subset or not. Start from one subset, the empty one, and decide the values one at a time.

When you reach a new value, every subset built so far has a twin that also contains it. You can grow the answer by copying each existing subset and adding the value to the copy, or recurse with an include/skip choice.

Copy each subset before changing it so the results never share a list. The answer itself holds 2^k subsets, so the work is proportional to its size; the probe doubles the number of subsets n = 2^k. Intended complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n log n) space in the number of subsets n, which is O(k * 2^k) for k values.
inputSyntax: Input: the values as a list, for example: [1, 2, 3]
